wiki_catalogs.name: Project Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for this section focused on the mcp-crawl4ai-rag project. Explain its purpose as a backend implementation providing web crawling and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) capabilities for AI agents via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Detail the vision of enabling AI systems to dynamically extend their knowledge by crawling, indexing, and querying external content. Describe the core architecture involving Crawl4AI for scraping, Supabase for vector storage, and Neo4j for knowledge graph integration. Highlight key features such as contextual embeddings, hybrid search, agentic RAG, hallucination detection, and modular tool registration. Include high-level diagrams illustrating system context and data flow. Provide beginner-friendly explanations of MCP, RAG, and knowledge graphs while also offering technical depth for advanced users. Reference real-world use cases like AI coding assistants and documentation-aware chatbots.

wiki_overview.content:
<blog>
# Comprehensive Project Analysis: Crawl4AI RAG MCP Server

## Project Introduction

### Purpose Statement
The Crawl4AI RAG MCP Server is a sophisticated implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that integrates web crawling capabilities with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to empower AI agents and AI coding assistants. The system enables AI models to scrape web content, store it in a vector database, and perform semantic searches over the crawled knowledge, effectively extending their contextual awareness beyond their training data.

### Core Goals and Objectives
1. **Web Crawling Integration**: Provide AI agents with the ability to crawl websites, documentation, and code repositories to gather up-to-date information.
2. **Advanced RAG Capabilities**: Implement sophisticated retrieval strategies including contextual embeddings, hybrid search, agentic RAG, reranking, and knowledge graph integration to enhance search precision and relevance.
3. **AI Hallucination Detection**: Utilize Neo4j knowledge graphs to validate AI-generated code against real repository structures, detecting non-existent methods, incorrect parameters, and other hallucinations.
4. **Flexible Deployment**: Support both Docker and direct Python execution with comprehensive configuration options for different embedding providers and AI services.

### Target Audience
- **AI Developers and Researchers**: Building AI agents that require access to current web content and documentation.
- **AI Coding Assistants**: Developers creating tools that help programmers by providing accurate code examples and validating generated code.
- **MCP Ecosystem Contributors**: Developers working with Model Context Protocol implementations who need robust web crawling and RAG capabilities.
- **Technical Teams**: Organizations that want to integrate AI assistants with their internal documentation and codebases.

## Technical Architecture

### Component Breakdown
The project follows a modular architecture with distinct components handling different aspects of the crawling, indexing, and retrieval pipeline:

- **Core MCP Server**: The main entry point that exposes tools to AI agents via the Model Context Protocol.
- **Web Crawling Engine**: Built on Crawl4AI, responsible for extracting content from websites using both static and dynamic (JavaScript-enabled) crawling.
- **Vector Database**: Supabase with pgvector extension for storing and retrieving embedded content.
- **Knowledge Graph System**: Neo4j-based graph database for storing code structure and enabling AI hallucination detection.
- **Chunking and Processing**: Advanced text and code chunking strategies to optimize content for retrieval.
- **Embedding Generation**: Support for multiple embedding providers including OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, and local Qwen models.

### Design Patterns
The system employs several key design patterns:

- **Dependency Injection**: The `crawl4ai_lifespan` function manages the lifecycle of core components and injects them into the request context.
- **Modular Architecture**: Clear separation between crawling, storage, retrieval, and validation components.
- **Configuration-Driven**: Extensive use of environment variables to control behavior without code changes.
- **Asynchronous Processing**: Built on async/await patterns for efficient handling of I/O operations.

### System Relationships
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[AI Agent] --> B[MCP Server]
    B --> C[Web Crawler]
    B --> D[Supabase Vector DB]
    B --> E[Neo4j Knowledge Graph]
    C --> F[Website Content]
    D --> G[Semantic Search]
    E --> H[Code Validation]
    G --> I[Retrieved Content]
    H --> J[Hallucination Report]
    I --> A
    J --> A
```

### Data Flow Diagram
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User Request] --> B{URL Type?}
    B -->|Sitemap| C[Parse Sitemap]
    B -->|Text File| D[Extract URLs]
    B -->|Webpage| E[Smart Crawl]
    C --> F[URL List]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G[Web Crawler]
    G --> H[Raw Content]
    H --> I[Content Chunking]
    I --> J[Embedding Generation]
    J --> K[Supabase Storage]
    K --> L[Vector Index]
    M[User Query] --> N[Semantic Search]
    N --> L
    L --> O[Relevant Chunks]
    O --> P[Response Generation]
    P --> Q[AI Agent]
```

## Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- `src/crawl4ai_mcp.py`: The main MCP server implementation that handles all tool registrations and request processing.
- `mcp.json`: Configuration file that defines the MCP server endpoints.
- `Dockerfile`: Containerization configuration for easy deployment.

### Core Modules
- `src/utils.py`: Utility functions for Supabase interaction, document processing, and code example extraction.
- `knowledge_graphs/`: Collection of modules for knowledge graph operations including repository parsing and hallucination detection.
- `src/user_manual_chunker/`: Advanced chunking strategies for processing documentation and code.

### Configuration Approach
- `.env` file: Primary configuration mechanism using environment variables.
- `pyproject.toml`: Python package and dependency management.
- Feature flags: Configuration options like `USE_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH`, `USE_RERANKING`, and `USE_AGENTIC_RAG` enable/disable advanced features.

### External Dependencies
- `pyproject.toml`: Defines all external Python dependencies including Crawl4AI, Supabase, Neo4j, and sentence-transformers.
- `uv.lock`: Lock file ensuring consistent dependency versions.

### Integration Points
- **MCP Clients**: Integration with various MCP-compatible AI agents through SSE or stdio transport.
- **Supabase**: Vector database for RAG storage and retrieval.
- **Neo4j**: Knowledge graph database for code structure storage and validation.
- **AI Providers**: Support for OpenAI and GitHub Copilot for embeddings and chat completions.

### Component Relationship Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
    A[MCP Server] --> B[Web Crawler]
    A --> C[Supabase]
    A --> D[Neo4j]
    A --> E[Embedding Provider]
    B --> F[Website]
    C --> G[Vector Search]
    D --> H[Code Validation]
    E --> I[Embeddings]
    G --> A
    H --> A
    I --> C
```

## Key Features

### Functionality Overview
The Crawl4AI RAG MCP Server provides a comprehensive suite of tools for AI agents:

1. **Web Crawling Tools**: `crawl_single_page` and `smart_crawl_url` for extracting content from websites.
2. **RAG Search**: `perform_rag_query` for semantic search over crawled content with optional source filtering.
3. **Knowledge Graph Tools**: `parse_github_repository`, `check_ai_script_hallucinations`, and `query_knowledge_graph` for code analysis and validation.
4. **Source Management**: `get_available_sources` to list available data sources for filtering.

### Implementation Highlights
- **Smart URL Detection**: Automatically identifies URL types (sitemap, text file, regular webpage) and applies appropriate crawling strategy.
- **Parallel Processing**: Efficiently crawls multiple pages simultaneously to improve performance.
- **Content Chunking**: Intelligently splits content by headers and size for better processing and retrieval.
- **Hybrid Search**: Combines vector and keyword search for more comprehensive results.
- **Agentic RAG**: Specialized code example extraction and storage for AI coding assistants.
- **Reranking**: Improves result relevance using cross-encoder models.

### Feature Architecture Diagram
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Initialization
    Initialization --> Ready: Configuration Loaded
    Ready --> Crawling: crawl_single_page/smart_crawl_url
    Crawling --> Processing: Content Extracted
    Processing --> Chunking: Split Content
    Chunking --> Embedding: Generate Embeddings
    Embedding --> Storage: Save to Supabase
    Ready --> Searching: perform_rag_query
    Searching --> Retrieval: Find Relevant Chunks
    Retrieval --> Reranking: Improve Relevance
    Reranking --> Response: Return Results
    Ready --> KnowledgeGraph: parse_github_repository
    KnowledgeGraph --> Analysis: Extract Code Structure
    Analysis --> Neo4j: Store in Graph DB
    Ready --> Validation: check_ai_script_hallucinations
    Validation --> Reporting: Generate Hallucination Report
    Response --> Ready
    Reporting --> Ready
    Storage --> Ready
```

Sources:
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)
- [Dockerfile](Dockerfile)
- [mcp.json](mcp.json)
- [README.md](README.md)
- [src/crawl4ai_mcp.py](src/crawl4ai_mcp.py)
- [knowledge_graphs/knowledge_graph_validator.py](knowledge_graphs/knowledge_graph_validator.py)
- [knowledge_graphs/parse_repo_into_neo4j.py](knowledge_graphs/parse_repo_into_neo4j.py)
- [knowledge_graphs/hallucination_reporter.py](knowledge_graphs/hallucination_reporter.py)
- [tests/test_neo4j_integration.py](tests/test_neo4j_integration.py)
</blog>
